_meta.title: Instruction Cues — writer-instruction detection vocabulary
_meta.purpose: The shared cue list from Tag_Interpretation_Rules.md §2.3b, surfaced as data so extending instruction detection is a data edit, never a code change. Both the JS engine (TagNormaliser.js) AND the Python reference harness (reference/tests/normaliser.py) now BUILD their cue/addressee regexes from THIS file (round 10), so a single edit here updates both — no hand-sync, no drift.
_meta.how_used: Two checks, applied by TagNormaliser.js: (1) ADDRESSEE — if a bracket fragment OPENS with one of addressee_prefixes followed by one of addressee_separators, the whole fragment is a writer instruction (never tag-matched inside). (2) CUES — if no fragment resolved to a tag, the folded span is scanned for any cue_patterns match (word-boundary regex); a hit classifies the span as a writer instruction → red flag (§4.1).
_meta.extension_rule: New instruction phrasing observed in a template = append ONE pattern here. Never add a per-tag rule in code. After editing, re-run reference/tests/run_regression.py (coverage must stay >= 99.9%).
_meta.pattern_syntax: cue_patterns entries are regex FRAGMENTS, joined by the engine with | inside \b( ... )\b. Plain words are safe; '.' matches any char (e.g. 'right.hand column' covers 'right-hand' and 'right hand').
